Alex K: Heads-up — I saw a 15–20% throughput regression on the 8k-token benchmark for the 4xA100 job after the fused-attn kernel landed. Profiling attached in-thread, but initial sign is more GPU idle in backward.
Maria S: :eyes: any idea if it's compute or all-reduce related? nvlink topology changed for that test cluster last week.
Taj R: Can you paste the timeline? if compute drops and all-reduce spikes it could be NCCL graph change or increased comm/compute sync.
Alex K: Posting the micro-timeline I grabbed with nvprof/nsight (trimmed):
```
0.00s compute attention fwd GPU0
0.01s compute fwd GPU0
0.12s allreduce grad0 GPU0 -> GPU1 (start)
0.18s allreduce grad0 (end)
0.19s compute backward GPU0
0.22s idle GPU0  <-- increased gap vs before
```
Before the kernel change the allreduce overlapped with the next compute chunk; now there's a barrier.
perf-bot: CI perf/regression: throughput -18% on 4xA100 (job id perf/2026-03-05-44). See perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/jobs/2026-03-05-44
Priya V: Did the fused-attn kernel introduce an implicit cudaDeviceSynchronize or a blocking stream? I remember a PR that switched some kernels to default stream.
Alex K: Good call — the new kernel uses cuBLASLt on the default stream for GEMM when workspace not set, which can force sync across streams. That would kill async NCCL overlap.
Sam J: NVLINK topology also matters: if some GPUs are not NVLINK-connected (PCIe hop), NCCL falls back to ring algorithm with extra hops and latency. Can you confirm the node topology with `nvidia-smi topo -m`?
Alex K: Ran it: GPUs 0-1 NVLink, 2-3 NVLink, but 1 <-> 2 is only PCIe. On our previous cluster we had a full mesh NVLink on that SKU. So two factors: kernel default stream sync + partial NVLink graph.
Taj R: Two experiments to isolate:
1) force the fused kernel onto a non-default stream / set cublasLT to use non-blocking path (if possible) and rerun. Should restore overlap.
2) run same job on full-mesh NVLink node (if available in infra) and see if regression disappears.
Maria S: I can repro on infra-qa-4xA100 with PCIe middle hop. I'll spin up a run on nvlink-mesh nodes (rack-2) and post results.
Alex K: Quick patch I tried locally: set `STREAMS_COMPAT=1` and use our pinned compute stream for fused-attn. Throughput before: 152 tokens/s, after patch: 180 tokens/s (baseline before regression 185). So mostly recovered.
Priya V: Nice. For long term we should ensure kernels never use default stream implicitly. Add a check in kernel selection to prefer our exec stream and warn if fallback to default.
Taj R: Also consider topology-aware tensor/pipeline parallel placement. If pipeline boundaries end up across PCIe hops you'll pay double for KV-cache syncs and all-reduce. We should update the placement heuristic to prefer NVLink-connected peers for pipeline stages when possible.
Sam J: We can expose topology info to the scheduler via `nvidia-smi topo -m` parsing during node init and set a rank affinity graph for NCCL. Also EFA/InfiniBand RDMA with GPUDirect could bypass PCIe for cross-node comms — but only helps across hosts, not intra-node PCIe hops.
Alex K: Another perf wrinkle: KV cache fetches are sharded per-GPU; we were doing an extra rendezvous for cross-GPU cache lookups which shows up as latency tail on long contexts. If pipeline stage placement splits sequence dims across PCIe hops that tail amplifies.
Maria S: Notes from my run on nvlink-mesh: regression disappears (throughput ~184 tokens/s). On PCIe-middle nodes it's still ~150. So both kernel sync and topology amplify each other.
Priya V: Action items:
- Priya: add guard to kernel selection to avoid default-stream blocking and add unit test. (PR: #alpha)
- Taj: prototype topology-aware placement in dev branch, try greedy NVLink-first placement. (branch: topology-placement)
- Maria: run a set of canary jobs across node types and capture nvprof traces. Upload traces to perf dashboard.
- Sam: add node topo metadata to cluster inventory and expose to scheduler.
Alex K: Also flagged a perf regression issue: PERF-679 in Jira with traces and before/after numbers.
Taj R: For multi-GPU comm tuning, let's experiment with NCCL envs: NCCL_ALGO=Ring or Tree, NCCL_NTHREADS, and NCCL_COMM_ID mapping. In some partial-mesh topologies Tree helps reduce latency spikes.
Priya V: Will add a warning in our runtime when `kernel->uses_default_stream == true` and make default-stream usage fatal in tests.
Sam J: FYI, InfiniBand/EFA notes: enable GPUDirect RDMA and pinned memory to reduce host memcpy. For cross-host allreduce, EFA latency << TCP. But intra-node NVLink still best for GPU-to-GPU.
Alex K: TL;DR: regression root cause = fused-attn kernel using default/blocking stream + partial NVLink topology causing poor NCCL overlap. Short-term patch to pin kernel streams recovers most perf; medium-term: topology-aware placement + scheduler metadata + safer kernel selection.
Maria S: I'll create the canary matrix (node types x model sizes x batch configs) and post results by EOD.
perf-bot: Note: rolling canary scheduled for 2026-03-07 02:00 UTC covering nvlink-mesh and pcie-middle node pools.
Alex K: Thanks all — will open PR for the kernel guard and link here. :thumbsup:
